analysis.r6_router_paths: m=1: rr<1,1>, FP32 weights read directly. 256 CTAs x 512 thr, 1 row x full K per CTA, 64 B in flight per thread at launch, in-CTA shuffle/smem reduce, no cross-CTA step. Kernel 2.9 us, judge 4.14. m=8/16: gv<2,MT,2,1,8,2,8> (c8): bf16 hi+lo fragments (8.4 MB), 16 rows x K/8 per CTA, 8 warps x KU=2, so every W byte and x chunk is requested in the first ~60 instructions. Then one 16-deep dependent HMMA chain per n8 tile (hi and lo accumulate into one register set; NC=1), an STS / BAR / LDS in-CTA reduce over WK=8, a cluster barrier, 8 DSMEM loads per output, STG of fp32, and a second cluster barrier. 128 CTAs, cluster 8. m=32: gv<2,4,2,1,4,2,16> (c16): 256 CTAs x 128 thr, cluster 16.
analysis.m_independent: In-prepare (offset-subtracted) bake lines, three runs: rr 3.2 at m=1 vs gv c8 4.2-4.3 at m=1 and m=8, with the same bytes and negligible x. So gv's structure costs about 1.0 us over rr: cluster launch, two cluster barriers, the DSMEM gather and the in-CTA BAR plus 8-way smem reduce, and the 16-deep HMMA chain (about 16 x ~33 cycles = 0.27 us; SASS: 16 HMMAs into R8). rr itself sits about 0.7 us above 8.4 MB / 3.8 TB/s, which is one DRAM latency plus launch, with the whole matrix requested at t=0. That part is not attackable without fewer bytes, and the 12-bit pair lost 1.6 us to decode on the critical path (pw11). The judge adds a further ~1.2 us over kernel time for router-sized launches (2.9 -> 4.14), on every path.
analysis.m_dependent: gv c8: 4.2 (m=8) -> 4.4 (m=16) -> 8.1 (m=32). c16 at m=32: 5.0-5.2. Two parts. (a) x is re-fetched by every 16-row tile, so x L2 traffic is 16 x m x 8192 x 2 B = 2 / 4 / 8.4 MB at m=8/16/32, against 8.4 MB of W. It is requested in the same first round trip, and at m=32 it doubles the bytes moved; HMMA count also grows 16 -> 64 per warp, which is issue only, since the chain depth stays 16. (b) c8 at m=32 needs 152 regs, so 1 CTA/SM; 128 CTAs in clusters of 8 exceed the 120 co-resident (pw11's guard), so a second wave forms. That is why r6 switches to c16 at m=32.
analysis.rejected_candidates: (i) more CTAs with smaller K slices: r6 already has every W byte in flight at launch (KU=2=ST), and its own KU=1 geometry (1,8,1,16) is 1.5-2 us slower at m=1/8/32 in all three logs. (iii) interleaved hi/lo: all 16 W loads are issued in the first ~60 instructions, so instruction count is not on the critical path. (iv) the FP32 output is already written by the cluster gather with no extra pass.

claim: Six variants on r6's router kernel (FMT 2, same loads, same reduction): gr-c8n / gr-c16n put hi and lo in separate accumulators (V bit 18: two interleaved 8-deep HMMA chains, then 4 FADDs; SASS-checked), shortening the chain by about 0.13 us. gr-c8b / gr-c8bn cap c8 at 128 regs (minBlocks 2) so 128 CTAs co-reside at m=32 with no second wave. gr-c16w / gr-c16wn give 32 rows per CTA at m=32 (128 CTAs x 256 thr), halving the x re-read from 8.4 to 4.2 MB. The cluster-16 residency guard may decline these at 1 CTA/SM.
paths: m=1/8/16: gr-c8n, gr-c16n. m=32: gr-c16n, gr-c8b, gr-c8bn, gr-c16w, gr-c16wn. PROBE rtr router m=1 / m=32 pair the best gr path with r6 (3 x 21 replays, alternated), in the gvbulk/xpol line format. pw16's gc paths are removed; pw11's gx paths and gb-q-n4 stay.
kill_if: Kill the r6-structure router line if no router m=32 gr path is at least 0.8 us under the 'r6' line in the same bake. In that case the m-independent ~1.0 us of gv over rr (cluster + barriers + reduce) is the only remaining pool. The next step there is a structural change, not a variant: x as the mma A operand and W rows as B (n8 tiles), W slice bulk-loaded to smem at launch, 32-64 CTAs, cluster-2 or no reduction.
